sanjay: Heads-up — noticed a weird divergence: p99 on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate jumped to ~1.2s but the endpoint breakdown p99 is still ~700ms. Anyone seen this after the quota routing change?
elaine: link? and which dashboard view (global p99 vs per-route rollup)?
sanjay: console link: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/latency?endpoint=%2Fv1%2Fgenerate — root query looks like this:
```
SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 0.99) AS p99 FROM traces
WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND ts > now() - 1h
GROUP BY route
```
The rollup widget (top-level) shows p99=1200ms, route breakdown rows all show ~650-800ms.
maria: my guess: sampling/provenance mismatch. Dashboard top-level rollup uses the rollout-sampled stream (includes fallback variant routing weights) while the endpoint table is using raw trace origin (only requests handled by that variant). If routing weight shifted to a slower fallback but samples are biased, percentiles can diverge.
elaine: that makes sense. Did we change the routing policy recently? Tyler/infra — any quota or route_weight changes around 1707778800?
tyler: deploy-bot shows a policy tweak at 1707778800 (quota-routing: increase fallback weight for over-quota clients). deploy-bot: "quota-routing v2 applied by ops@tyler at 1707778800".
deploy-bot: POLICY_CHANGE: quota-routing v2 -> increased fallback weight 0.10 -> 0.30 for high-volume keys.
sanjay: OK that aligns. But UI should make this obvious — users see the top rollup but have no provenance visibility for that percentile. I toggled "show sample origin" and when I include the rollout-sampled origin the p99 moves to match the top-level.
maria: Right — root cause is merge semantics. Our rollup pipeline currently blends samples by route weight but the endpoint breakdown query uses per-route unmerged samples. Two different contracts. We need a clear contract: either rollups must include sample counts + merge_mode metadata or the console must label which origin is being displayed.
elaine: short-term: can we add sample_count to the endpoint table and a tiny provenance pill (origin=raw|rollout|cache) next to percentiles?
tyler: I can do a small metrics-api change to return sample_count + origin for each percentile bucket. Plan: add fields `sample_count` and `provenance` to the /v1/metrics/percentile response. Will open PR and canary.
maria: also request to metrics ingestion: add `weighted_percentile` as optional field so rollups that apply route_weighting can expose both raw and weighted p99s. That way console can show both numbers and a tooltip explaining when they diverge.
sanjay: UX suggestion: show p50/p95/p99 with small subline: "provenance: rollout-sampled (n=123k) • weighted_p99=1.2s • raw_p99=700ms" and a hover explaining sampling origin and routing policy. Saves a ton of confusion.
elaine: agree. Also we should add an alert rule: if weighted_p99 / raw_p99 > 1.25 then flag and auto-open a ticket to platform.
tyler: open PR #1287 (draft) for the metrics-api change and a small console patch to show the provenance pill. Will canary to 10% of orgs.
maria: pinging telemetry team for contract update: we need explicit docs on merge_mode semantics (none, weighted, fallback-first) and guarantees about sample_count accuracy. Otherwise users will be chasing ghosts.
sanjay: thanks — for now I'm adding a note in the dashboard description to call out the difference. After PR lands let's re-evaluate the p99 delta. :thumbsup:
elaine: thanks team. small follow-up: can someone add a short snippet to the rollout playbook about checking sample origin when p99 jumps? saves on-boarding time.
tyler: will do. PR + playbook update by EOD.
deploy-bot: NOTE: route_policy change was rolled out at 1707778900 to 30% of traffic.
